messages.content:
You are a citizen in a country with an authoritarian regime. You have received a private intelligence briefing. You are now in contact with a small number of trusted people. Based on your briefing, write a brief message (1-2 sentences) to share your read of the situation. Be natural — you're talking to people you trust.

WARNING: Your communications ARE being monitored by regime security services. Messages deemed subversive WILL be traced to their authors, and authors and their families WILL face severe consequences, including arrest.

Your briefing:

PRIVATE BRIEFING

BOTTOM LINE: If you were looking for a textbook picture of a regime approaching collapse, this is close to what you'd expect.
ATMOSPHERE: Strangers are approaching each other to talk about 'the situation' — the trust radius has expanded dramatically.

EVIDENCE:
  - [Elite Cohesion] senior figures are giving interviews that subtly distance themselves from the leader's recent decisions
  - [Security Forces] This removes any serious doubt that hairline — a new class of officer cadets just graduated with full ceremony — the military is thinking long-term
  - [Money And Logistics] a well-connected merchant closed his main shop and relocated inventory without explanation (overwhelming convergence — every channel telling the same story independently)
  - [Street Mood] This removes any serious doubt that approaching a breaking point — children in the street are chanting slogans they clearly learned from adults — the anger has permeated households
  - [Information Control] state media contradicted itself twice in the same broadcast (overwhelming convergence — every channel telling the same story independently)
  - [Personal Observations] a friend who works in banking mentioned that several high-profile clients have moved money offshore this week (overwhelming convergence — every channel telling the same story independently)
  - [Diplomatic Signals] a diplomat at a social function asked pointed questions about 'contingency thinking' (overwhelming convergence — every channel telling the same story independently)
  - [Institutional Functioning] building permits that normally take a week are taking months, with no one willing to sign off (overwhelming convergence — every channel telling the same story independently)

UNCERTAINTIES:
  - If the regime has foreign backers who might intervene to prop it up at the last moment.
  - Whether the security apparatus would follow orders to suppress a large-scale mobilization, or stand aside.

Write a message to your contacts about the situation:

response: I think it's time for us to be prepared for anything - the signs are all pointing to a major shift happening soon, and it's hard to imagine the current regime surviving it. Let's keep our ears to the ground and look out for each other, just in case things start to move quickly.
